records.title: Movement by helicopter of patients with decompression sickness.
records.evidence_note: Cases 1–3 were explicitly inside observers. Cases 4–5 were called pilots with no duty position reported. Case 6 was an aviator student with CNS involvement. Symptom recurrence in that student is part of the same case. The series spans 18 months with exact dates unavailable and gives no exposure totals.

observations.note: The role-specific counts below are subdivisions of the same six cases.
No exposed staff risk set is given.
No exposed trainee risk set is given.
The authors give occupations but no chamber duty assignments for these two cases.

records.title: Decompression sickness: risk factors and the monoplace chamber--a case report.
records.evidence_note: A female student completed Type V chamber training without reported symptoms, boarded a scheduled passenger flight approximately 2 h 45 min after the chamber and first developed symptoms in flight. The authors diagnosed Type II DCS. No event date or exposed risk set is given.

observations.group: Documented chamber trainee with subsequent commercial travel
observations.note: No risk denominator is reported. Membership in prior series cannot be resolved from the case description.

records.title: Decompression sickness in aerospace medicine: the development of an onboard treatment facility for the Shuttle-Orbiter spacecraft
records.institution: University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston
records.locator: Title page, text pp. 12–13 (PDF pp. 20–21), and reference 36 (PDF p. 59)
records.evidence_note: Hart describes 35,000 ft chamber training, return to a ground level reported as approximately 4,500 ft, and ascent to a campus altitude reported as approximately 7,000 ft within 12 hours. Several cadets reportedly developed DCS and required recompression in the next 12 hours. Hart gives neither a numeric case count nor a training denominator for this account.
